text:
devon: FYI dependabot flagged a critical libsodium CVE (CVE-2026-9999) used by kms-agent and private runtime. Need patch schedule + customer comms. Risk: remote key extraction if attacker can reach KMS node. Who can triage exploitability?

maria: Do we have a public exploit PoC? Any active scans? If not, still treat as high because libsodium is crypto.

kevin: No PoC yet. Vendor says 'high' with CVSS 8.2. Our preliminary build shows only KMS agent server-side code links to libsodium via native wheel.

sam: Suggest staggered rollout: Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private. Hosted patch 24h canary, wait 6h, then Dedicated 48h rolling, then provide patch bundle + docs for Private customers. That reduces SLA risk.

alice: SLA question: for Dedicated customers committed to reserved capacity, do we have to notify for scheduled downtime? Some contracts require 72h notice for interruptive maintenance.

devon: Good point. Non-disruptive patching possible for most nodes (hot-reload is available). Only air-gapped Private on-prem may require manual OS-level lib replacement.

maria: Can we produce a heatmap of customer exposure by tier? I can pull which clusters use the legacy kms-agent image.

kevin: I'll run a quick inventory: `kubectl get pods -n redwood | grep kms-agent` then map images. Expect list in ~2h.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy started at 2004123500 for hosted/kms-agent:v1.4.3 -> v1.4.4 :rocket:

sam: If canary passes, schedule hosted full rollout in 8h. Notify security@ and customers@. For Dedicated, schedule maintenance window next Tue 01:00 UTC, give customers choice to opt out.

alice: For Private customers, prepare backport package + SHA sums and a short runbook. Also a KB article on why upgrade matters (no jargon).

devon: I'll draft comms for enterprise CS. Maria/Kevin pls add exposure heatmap + inventory. Can we aim to close triage + staged rollout plan by EOD?

maria: On it. Kevin and I will sync in 30.

kevin: syncing now. ping if you need the query used.

devon: thanks team. tagging @security-leads for visibility. :lock:
